description: The team is interested in making an app that will update us with real-life information about our earth
summary:
Designed like an effortless "information jukebox," OrbitPulse requires zero search bars or technical setup. The moment the app opens, five automated trackers sync live data from NASA, NOAA, and ESA, translating raw numbers into plain-English alerts and visual gauges:
• 01 Solar Flares — Earth Impact: Monitors real-time X-ray flux and planetary Kp-index data from NOAA SWPC to display an Earth Impact Threat Gauge alongside plain-English status briefings for GPS, satellites, power grids, and aurora visibility.
• 02 Asteroids & Comets: Cross-references live feeds from NASA JPL CNEOS and ESA's NEO Coordination Centre to track close-approach near-Earth objects, showing exact lunar miss distances and hazard ratings.
• 03 Artemis • Moon • Mars: Pulls real-time deep-space exploration milestones directly from NASA's Artemis and Mars Curiosity mission portals.
• 04 Rocket Launches: Aggregates live global launch countdowns, launch pad details, and payload summaries from SpaceX and the NextSpaceflight API.
• 05 Earth Events: Combines live satellite alerts from NASA EONET and NASA FIRMS active fire feeds—complete with an instant India regional filter—and NASA's GEDI Global Forest Canopy Height visualization (SVS ID: 4950) to highlight wildfires, severe storms, and ecosystem risks.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

OrbitPulse is an autonomous Space and Earth Mission Control dashboard built for the Earth Information Jukebox challenge. Instead of forcing users to write technical queries or dig through separate agency portals, OrbitPulse works like a real-time space and Earth jukebox—the moment the app loads, five automated trackers sync live telemetry from NASA, NOAA, and ESA and translate raw scientific feeds into plain-English situational awareness:

  • 01 Solar Flares — Earth Impact: Pulls real-time X-ray flux and planetary Kp-index data from NOAA’s Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC) to calculate a visual Earth Impact Threat Gauge and generate plain-English status cards for GPS, satellites, power grids, and aurora visibility.
  • 02 Asteroids & Comets: Cross-references live close-approach data from NASA JPL CNEOS and ESA’s NEO Coordination Centre to track near-Earth objects passing by this week, displaying lunar miss distances, speeds, and hazard ratings.
  • 03 Artemis • Moon • Mars: Aggregates live deep-space mission updates and milestones directly from NASA’s official Artemis and Mars Science (Curiosity rover) portals.
  • 04 Rocket Launches: Streams global launch countdowns, launch pad locations, and payload summaries from SpaceX and the NextSpaceflight API.
  • 05 Earth Events: Combines real-time satellite natural event feeds from NASA EONET and NASA FIRMS active fire data—featuring an instant India regional filter—alongside NASA’s GEDI Global Forest Canopy Height visualization (SVS ID: 4950) to highlight wildfires, severe storms, and ecosystem risks.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Zero-Friction Access: Removes intimidating search bars, raw JSON feeds, and scientific jargon so anyone can understand live space and Earth data in seconds.
  • Unified Situational Awareness: Consolidates five distinct space weather, planetary defense, exploration, launch, and Earth observation feeds into one cohesive mission control screen.
  • Verified Scientific Trust: Every single tracker displays live retrieval timestamps and direct clickable source URLs to official NASA, NOAA, and ESA endpoints so users can verify the underlying data.
  • Regional & Global Relevance: Built-in regional toggles (such as the dedicated India filter on the Earth Events tab) allow users to switch effortlessly between global trends and local environmental alerts.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

OrbitPulse bridges the gap between world-class space agency data and everyday public understanding. Our intended impact is to serve as an accessible early-warning and educational hub for students, educators, local communities, and disaster planners—empowering people to monitor solar storms affecting communication networks, track nearby wildfires or severe cyclones in real time, and stay connected to humanity's ongoing exploration of the Moon and Mars.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • AI App Development & Hosting Platform: Base44 (used to architect, generate, and deploy the full-stack web application at spectacular-orbit-pulse-live.base44.app).
  • Frontend & Logic Stack: React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and automated LLM + Live Web Search agents for real-time data retrieval, parsing, and plain-English summarization.
  • Open Space & Earth Data Sources: NASA EONET API, NASA FIRMS, NASA Scientific Visualization Studio (GEDI Forest Height ID: 4950), NASA JPL CNEOS, NASA Artemis & Mars Science feeds, NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC), ESA NEO Coordination Centre, SpaceX, and NextSpaceflight.
  • Hardware & Media Production Tools: Standard laptops (Chromebook) and mobile devices (Vivo smartphone) for development, testing, screen recording, and video editing.

5. How is your project creative?

Most space apps either display static educational text or overwhelm users with complex scientific charts meant only for experts. We reimagined The Earth Information Jukebox as a sleek, dark-mode Mission Control Jukebox where users simply "tune into" five live planetary and cosmic channels with a single click. Pairing real-time NOAA solar telemetry and NASA EONET disaster tracking with NASA’s 3D GEDI Forest Canopy Height visualization creates a unique storytelling link—showing not just where wildfires are burning today, but also the global forest ecosystems at stake.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Accessibility & Usability: We deliberately eliminated open-ended prompt bars so non-technical users, students, and busy emergency responders get instant answers the moment the page opens.
  • Data Accuracy & Anti-Hallucination: Because AI summaries can sometimes misstate live numbers, we engineered every module to display a Verified Live Sources footer with exact retrieval timestamps and direct links to official NASA, NOAA, and ESA endpoints.
  • Visual Clarity & Hierarchy: We designed a high-contrast dark-space UI with color-coded severity badges (Low, Moderate, Severe), threat gauges, and scannable briefing cards so critical risk levels stand out immediately on both desktop and mobile screens.
  • Local-to-Global Utility: Developing from India, we incorporated a dedicated India filter inside the Natural Events Network so local users can immediately spot regional cyclones or wildfires alongside global events.
